text.p: Tallinna Pank on Thursday denied reports that it plans to merge with any local banks but would continue to develop as a universal bank in the Baltics.
The bank was responding to earlier local media reports which said that Tallinna Pank and Hoiupank , the second largest bank, have started merger talks.

"The present strategy is to act as a separate universal bank in Estonia in the future in the whole of the Baltics and therefore we do not see any mergers with any other Estonian bank in the short term," Raus told a news conference.
Tallinna Pank's council and board have not given any authority to start official merger talks with an Estonian or a foreign financial institution, he added.
Raus earlier said that Tallinna Pank has agreed in principle to buy 100 percent of the shares of Latvia's Saules Bank, in which it already owns a 20 percent stake.
